subject: Linguistics
title: The Phoenician Alphabet
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Phoenician Alphabet usable.

hook.text: Around 1050 BCE, Phoenician merchants created 22 symbols—and changed literacy forever.

buildup.text: The Phoenician alphabet was the first widely used consonantal script—an abjad with no vowels.

discovery.text: It was simple enough for merchants to learn—no need for years of scribal training.

twist.text: The letter 'A' started as an ox head ('aleph') rotated upside down—the shape evolved over millennia.

climax.text: From Phoenician came Greek, Latin, Arabic, Hebrew, and almost every alphabet in use today.

punchline.text: Twenty-two letters launched a writing revolution.

quiz.question: What was the Phoenician alphabet originally designed for?
